input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The second Section 12.4 imposes a non-compete directly on Customer covering development, marketing, sale, and acquisition of any competing product or service, in any territory, for the term plus 24 months. That is both undefined in scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor") and a post-term restriction exceeding 12 months, hitting the walk-away position on two counts. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. Preferred position is no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer, so we delete the paragraph and offer the narrowed fallback in the comment.

proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month, all-territory non-compete imposed on Customer in the second Section 12.4.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted this provision: we cannot accept any non-compete or field-of-use restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build, and a 24-month post-term, all-territory restriction also directly contradicts Section 12.3. If Vendor needs protection for a specific offering, we could consider a restriction limited to a single named competing product, during the term only and no longer than 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
